newsitem.title: TURKEY: Burcelik to raise 1997 sales by 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Burcelik to raise 1997 sales by 12 pct.

text.p: Turkish cast steel, machinery, stainless steel and taps producer Burcelik Bursa Celik Dokum Sanayii A.S. aims to increase 1997 turnover by 12 percent from $9.5 million in 1996, a senior official said.
"We will be able to increase our total sales to around $11 million, if market conditions continue as they are in the first five months," Ragip Serdaroglu, president of the company, told Reuters.
Shares of the company closed at 15,750 lira on Monday, up from Friday's 15,500 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange.
Serdaroglu said their production programme was generally prepared parallel to orders and 45 percent of the output was exported to the European Union (EU) countries, the United States and Canada.

"We pay tax on earnings which are not real because our export revenues are converted to Turkish lira and seem higher because of the lira's depreciation against the dollar. So we do not want to raise the share of exports in total sales," Serdaroglu said.
Burcelik increased its total output by 13.5 percent to 1,896 tonnes in 1996 from 1,670 tonnes in 1995 and aims to raise it by 10-12 percent this year.
Capacity utilisation was more than 90 percent in 1996 and the company plans to increase output via new investments to overcome a bottleneck in processing molten steel.
Its molten steel capacity stands at 10,000 tonnes while processing capacity is far less at 2,000 tonnes, but will rise to 2,200 tonnes this year with the new investments.

Burcelik produces big pieces of cast steel, like rings of cement factory mills or crucibles of steel factories, each weighing 30 to 35 tonnes. Recently privatised Karabuk iron and steel plant is its only domestic rival in this field.
The company is one of the three producers of crushing-screening plants in Turkey, widely used in road building.

Last year, the company began to produce taps and various machinery parts from stainless steel, which is resistant to acids and widely used in the chemical industry, after four years of research and development.
Serdaroglu said they were strong in the EU market in taps and other cast steel products.
"Many cast plants were shut down and many others are planning to close in the near future in Europe, because of high labour costs and environmental problems," Serdaroglu said.
The company reported 790.2 billion lira of net sales and 87.3 trillion lira of net profits last year, against 429 billion and 57 billion in 1995.
